mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by 2% or more year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for 3 consecutive months by >1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 1% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher interest rates and inflation, which erodes corporate earnings and consumer purchasing power, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between housing starts (HOUST) and personal income (PAYEMS) over the past six months indicates robust household formation and income growth, which supports consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Pearson correlation(HOUST, PAYEMS) > 0.7 over last 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST and PAYEMS correlation exceeds 0.7 over the prior six months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM growth for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS grows by more than 0.5% month-over-month for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of 3% or more signals a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which directly reduces corporate sales and profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS declines by 3% or more year-over-year.
